title: Every framework request resolves the session twice: sys_session and sys_user are each read twice (9-13 SQL queries per request), one remote round trip each on Turso
body:
repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

Filing gate: ① a measured defect from step 1 of objectstack-ai/cloud#4563 (p1; a hosted page takes 9–10 s to open). Reader: the `domain:server` lane; the objectstack fleet dispatches its own cards. Dedupe: `getSession twice per request`, `sys_session read twice`, `identity prelude queries`, `per-request auth queries` — no open card.

## Measured

Cloud main `8431db621`, objectstack pin `1aac465fe1d0`, local prod-like stack, hosted posture, a plain owner, `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json`:
- Every framework request runs 9–13 SQL queries.
- `sys_session` by token and `sys_user` by id each appear twice per request.
- Two in-process `getSession` calls per request explain it:
  - the auth gate (runtime `http-dispatcher.ts`, near line 1665);
  - principal resolution (`security/resolve-session-principal.ts` line 64, reached from `dispatcher-plugin.ts` near line 217).
- On a remote Turso database each query is a round trip, so the duplicate adds two round trips to every request on hosted.
- Under a 28-request burst, auth goes from 7 to 227–263 ms (db about 1 ms locally) and get-session from 11 to 341 ms. That is queueing on one event loop, so per-request work multiplies with concurrency.

## Done when

One request resolves the session and the user once, and the result is shared by the auth gate and principal resolution. A test pins the query count of an authenticated request.
